stops.note: referred to a rich part of whale meat, later broadened to mean food or plenty
combined with 'hiyu' (plenty) to mean 'plenty to eat' in the Pacific Northwest trade language
folk-etymologized in English as 'high', producing a phrase for an important, self-important person

current_meaning: an important or self-important person, often used humorously, as in 'high muckamuck'
